chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Preferring small groups with minimal arrangements
summary: She felt boxed in singing with big-band arrangements.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Okay. You've told use earlier on that in general you prefer playing with a small group with a trio of quartet behind you than with a big band.

Yeah, well at this particular point I prefer practically no arrangements, no pre-set music because since I've come back as a jazz singer most jazz is sort of free form and I don't always wind up with the kind of instruments behind me that my arrangements might call for and I don't want to have to go through the business of transposing arrangements anymore because it's not the same. An arrangement is made for a certain instrumentation and it doesn't sound the same when it's played by other instruments.

So anyway, at the time then did you feel the same way?

Yeah, I've always felt a little boxed in when it comes to singing with big arrangements. And unless they were, the arrangements of my standard repertoire, you know, like "Loch Lomond" and "The Saint Louis Blues". And then you see too if you'll notice, this is a departure from the Swing-idiom, you know the little tight arrangements, you know, and the little carefully selected repertoires. It's just pop tunes.
